subject: Recap + next steps: feature economics & payback (cost targets)

Subject: Recap + next steps: feature economics & payback (cost targets)

Thanks again for the time this morning — quick recap and where I think we should land next.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary use case: contextual resume and chat helper inside the employer portal (in-product assist).
- Expected steady-state: ~200k active users, ~15k prompts/day initially, estimating ~450M tokens/month across prompts + responses.
- Target commercial ask: get an operating cost that lets you land a $/feature target and keep CAC payback < 9 months. You mentioned a target of roughly $12–$18 per 1M tokens as a back-of-envelope target for pricing discussions.

Immediate asks / next steps from us:
1) Confirm the volume profile above (avg tokens per session, peak distribution). If 450M/month is off, call it out.
2) We'll send a short unit-econ sketch ($/1M tokens -> $/feature) and a CAC-payback sensitivity table for your team to review.
3) If the economics look reasonable, propose a 45-min pricing workshop next Tue/Thu to align final target and SLA needs.

I’m attaching a short summary + a spreadsheet with a few cost scenarios. High level takeaway we expect we can get inference cost (raw) into the $6–$10 per 1M tokens range with batching + quantization on a production profile; your target of $12–$18 would allow margin for product & CS while meeting a 6–9 month payback depending on ARPU.

Note: Priya — copying you to add a short note on caching/tech levers that change the per-token math.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Thanks Marcus — useful recap. Couple clarifications from our side:
- The 450M/month is our optimistic steady-state in 12 months. For the first 3 months post-launch expect 120–180M/month.
- Typical session: ~120 tokens in prompt, ~300 tokens in generated response (so roughly 420 tokens/session).
- Budget range: our finance team gave us a working target of $10k–$25k/month for inference costs in year 1. That maps to a target price per 1M tokens of approx $10–$21 depending on volume profile.

Two asks for Marcus/Redwood before the workshop:
1) Can you show a $/feature row for both 'quick assist' (hit rate 40%) and 'full summary' (hit rate 10%)?
2) Please include CAC payback sensitivity: we assume CAC ~ $45/user (marketing + SDR) and aim for payback <= 9 months.

If you can send that by EOD tomorrow we'll prep numbers from our side and lock the workshop.

—Elena Ruiz
Head of Product, Nimble Health
elena.ruiz@nimblehealth.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodhq.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: feature economics & payback (cost targets)

Appreciate the clarity, Elena. Attached is a quick sketch (see feature-econ-summary.pdf) — excerpt below for visibility. I put conservative and aggressive rows so you can see sensitivity to tokens and tech levers.

Excerpt (per 1M tokens basis):
- Raw inference cost (no cache, baseline model): $11.80 / 1M tokens (conservative).
- Optimized inference cost (batching, quantized FP16->INT8 variant, prefix caching): $6.40 / 1M tokens (aggressive).

Feature mapping (assume 420 tokens/session):
- Quick assist (avg 40% of users trigger, 0.4 hits/user): cost per active user/month: 0.4 * 420 tokens * (1/1,000,000) * $X per 1M tokens => with $6.40/1M = $0.11/user-month; with $11.80/1M = $0.20/user-month.
- Full summary (10% hit rate): cost per active user/month: 0.1 * 420 / 1,000,000 * $X => $0.03–$0.05/user-month depending on cost scenario.

If we map to your CAC target:
- Using conservative cost ($11.80/1M), ARPU needed for 9-month payback (CAC $45) => ~$5.00/user-month (roughly).
- Using optimized cost ($6.40/1M), ARPU for 9-month payback drops to ~$2.75/user-month.

Notes: these omit SRE/infra overhead you may want to apportion; the attached spreadsheet has a tab that rolls up to $/feature and a sensitivity table for CAC payback across ARPU buckets.

Proposed next step: 45-min workshop — Tues Jul 6 or Thu Jul 8 (PST) to align final pricing band and SLA. Which works for your team?

Best,
Marcus

Quick technical notes to supplement the spreadsheet — these materially change the cost rows if Nimble adopts them early: 

- Prefix & KV caching: for conversational flows where the prompt includes company template/context, we often see 20–40% token reuse between requests. When possible to cache and reuse KV embeddings, effective billed tokens drop proportionally.
- Batching policy: continuous batching vs per-request reduces GPU overhead; for your 450M/month profile we estimate ~12–25% token-cost reduction depending on latency SLO.
- Model variants / quantization: serving an INT8 quantized variant for non-critical summaries can cut cost ~30–45% compared with full FP16 generator for heavy outputs. We recommend a mixed policy: summary -> quantized; assist (low-latency) -> FP16.
- Cold-start considerations: first 2–6 weeks will skew cost higher until caches warm and prefix reuse patterns emerge; plan conservatively for higher initial month.

I can add a scenario in the spreadsheet that includes 30% effective cache hit + quantized offload and publish that tab by EOD.
